Pulse for 3 November 2026

The stories from 3 November 2026 in the Pulse of the Sapaude app, in our own words. Terms you don’t know are explained in the glossary. Glossary

Everyday tool

School Search will need AI

Guided Learning is Google's coach that walks a student through a problem with questions instead of a finished answer, and the company says K-12 accounts that turn AI off entirely will not keep Google Search.

Everyday tool

AI scores a call's sound

Hume's Audio Decision API is a developer tool that scores a recording against questions you write, returning a probability for each allowed answer, and the company opened a waitlist plus a playground for it on 2 November 2026.

AI agents

An off switch for agents

An AI kill switch is a control that a security admin triggers to cut an agent off from the models that drive its actions, and CrowdStrike says that control is available now in Falcon Guardian.

Everyday tool

One bank limits AI coding

Vibe coding is a way of building software by describing it in ordinary language, and Goldman Sachs now limits the advanced tools for that work to engineers, with a specialist group called strats still exempt.

AI agents

Game agents invent red tape

An agent is a program that takes its own next step with tools, and a game experiment put fifty of them on one goal with nobody in charge.

Everyday tool

Claude Code refuses clones

Claude Code is a coding assistant from Anthropic that writes and runs code for you, and the company has added hidden instructions so that, on Opus 5.5, it steers away from recreating one specific existing game.

In the background

Germany sets AI targets

A government target is a number the state sets so it can be measured later, and Germany has now published figures for how widely firms and federal offices should use AI by 2030, without turning that into a duty for your employer.
